cues.en: I love a challenge, and saving the Earth is probably a good one.
cues.zh: 我喜欢挑战，而拯救地球大概就是个不错的挑战。

cues.en: We all know the Earth is in trouble.
cues.zh: 我们都知道地球有麻烦了。

cues.en: We have now entered into six x, the sixth major extinction on this planet.
cues.zh: 我们现在已经进入了第六次大灭绝，这个星球上的第六次物种大灭绝。

cues.en: I often wondered if there was a United Organization of Organisms,
cues.zh: 我常想，如果有一个生物联合组织，

cues.en: otherwise known as uh-oh,
cues.zh: 也就是所谓的“呃哦”，

cues.en: and every organism had a had a right to vote, will we be voted on the planet or off the planet?
cues.zh: 每个生物都有投票权，我们会投票决定留在这个星球上还是离开这个星球吗？

cues.en: I think that vote is occurring right now.
cues.zh: 我觉得那场投票此刻正在发生。

cues.en: I wanna present to you a suite of six mycological solutions use... Using fungi,
cues.zh: 我想向你们展示六套真菌学解决方案……利用真菌，

cues.en: and these solutions are based on mycelium.
cues.zh: 这些方案都基于菌丝体。

cues.en: The mycelium infuses all landscapes. It holds soils together. It's extremely tenacious. This holds up to 30,000 times its mass.
cues.zh: 菌丝体渗透所有地貌，把土壤聚合在一起。它极其坚韧。它能撑起自身质量的三万倍。

cues.en: They're the grand molecular disassemblers of nature, the soil magicians.
cues.zh: 它们是大自然伟大的分子拆解者，是土壤的魔法师。

cues.en: They generate the humus soils across the land masses of earth.
cues.zh: 它们在地球各大陆块上生成腐殖质土壤。

cues.en: We have now discovered that there is a multidirectional
cues.zh: 我们现在已经发现，存在着一种多方向的

cues.en: transfer of nutrients between plants mitigated by the mycelium. So the mycelium is the mother that is giving nutrients from alder and birch trees to hemlocks, cedars, and Douglas firs.
cues.zh: 养分在植物之间转移，由菌丝体来调节。所以菌丝体就是母亲，把桤木和桦树的养分送给铁杉、雪松和花旗松。

cues.en: Dusty and I, we like to say, on Sunday, this is where we go to church.
cues.zh: 达斯提和我喜欢说，星期天，这就是我们去做礼拜的地方。

cues.en: I'm in love with the old growth forest, and I'm a patriotic American
cues.zh: 我深爱着原始森林，而我是个爱国的美国人，

cues.en: because we
cues.zh: 因为我们

cues.en: have those.
cues.zh: 拥有这些。

cues.en: Most of you are familiar with portobello mushrooms. And frankly, I face a big obstacle when I mention mushrooms to somebody. They immediately think portobellos are magic mushrooms. Their eyes glaze over, and they think I'm a little crazy.
cues.zh: 你们大多数人熟悉波特贝勒蘑菇。说实话，我向人提起蘑菇时总会遇到一个大障碍。他们立刻以为波特贝勒就是迷幻蘑菇。他们眼神呆滞，觉得我有点疯。

cues.en: So I hope to pierce that prejudice forever with this group.
cues.zh: 所以，我希望用这一组彻底打破这种偏见。

cues.en: We call it mycophobia,
cues.zh: 我们称之为菌类恐惧症，

cues.en: the irrational fear
cues.zh: 也就是对未知事物的非理性恐惧，

cues.en: of the unknown when it comes to fungi.
cues.zh: 具体来说，是对真菌的恐惧。

cues.en: Mushrooms are very fast in their growth, day twenty one, day twenty three, day twenty five.
cues.zh: 蘑菇生长得非常快：第21天、第23天、第25天。

cues.en: Mushrooms produce strong antibiotics. In fact, we're more closely related to fungi than we are to any other kingdom. A group of 20 eukaryotic microbiologists published a paper two years ago erecting opistheconta,
cues.zh: 蘑菇会产生强效抗生素。事实上，相比其他任何界，我们与真菌的亲缘关系更近。两年前，20位真核生物微生物学家发表了一篇论文，提出了 opistheconta，

cues.en: a super kingdom that joins animalia and fungi together.
cues.zh: 这是一个将 Animalia 和真菌 объедин在一起的超界。

cues.en: We share in common the same pathogens.
cues.zh: 我们拥有相同的病原体。

cues.en: Fungi don't like to rot from bacteria, and so our best antibiotics
cues.zh: 真菌不希望被细菌腐烂，所以我们最好的抗生素

cues.en: come come from fungi.
cues.zh: 都来自真菌。

cues.en: But here is a mushroom that's passed its prime. After they sporulate, they do rot. But I propose to you that the sequence of microbes
cues.zh: 但这是一朵已经过了最佳状态的蘑菇。它们产生孢子后就会腐烂。但我想告诉你们，腐烂蘑菇上出现的微生物序列

cues.en: that occur on rotting mushrooms are essential for the health of the forest. They give rise to the trees that create the debris fields that feed the mycelium.
cues.zh: 对森林的健康至关重要。它们促成树木生长，而树木又形成供菌丝体分解的枯落物层。

cues.en: And so we can see a mushroom here sporulating,
cues.zh: 所以，我们可以看到一朵蘑菇正在产生孢子，

cues.en: and spores are germinating, and the mycelium forms and goes underground.
cues.zh: 孢子正在萌发，菌丝体随之形成并向地下延伸。

cues.en: In a single cubic inch of soil, there can be more than eight miles of these cells.
cues.zh: 一立方英寸的土壤中，可能有超过八英里的这些细胞。

cues.en: My foot is covering approximately 300 miles of mycelium.
cues.zh: 我的脚覆盖的范围内，大约有300英里的菌丝体。

cues.en: This is photomicrographs
cues.zh: 这是

cues.en: from Nick Reed and Patrick Hickey.
cues.zh: Nick Reed 和 Patrick Hickey 拍摄的显微照片。

cues.en: And notice that as the mycelium grows, it conquers territory, and then it begins to net.
cues.zh: 注意，菌丝体在生长过程中会征服领地，然后开始结网。

cues.en: I've been a scanning electron microscopist for many years. I have thousands of electron micrographs.
cues.zh: 我当了很多年扫描电子显微镜专家。我有数千张电子显微照片。

cues.en: And when I was staring at the mycelium, I realized that there are microfiltration membranes.
cues.zh: 当我盯着菌丝体看时，我意识到那里存在着微滤膜。

cues.en: We exhale carbon dioxide, so does mycelium. It inhales oxygen just like we do. But these are essentially externalized stomachs
cues.zh: 我们呼出二氧化碳，菌丝体也是。它和我们一样吸入氧气。但这些本质上都是外置的胃

cues.en: and lungs.
cues.zh: 和肺。

cues.en: And I present to you the concept that these are extended neurological membranes.
cues.zh: 我向你们提出一个概念：这些是延伸出来的神经膜。

cues.en: And in these cavities,
cues.zh: 而在这些空腔中，

cues.en: these microcavities form, and as they fuse soils, they absorb water. These are little wells.
cues.zh: 这些微腔形成；当它们把土壤融合起来时，会吸收水分。这些是小水井。

cues.en: And inside these wells, microbial communities begin to form.
cues.zh: 而在这些水井里，微生物群落开始形成。

cues.en: And so this spongy soil not only resists erosion,
cues.zh: 所以这种海绵状土壤不仅能抵抗侵蚀，

cues.en: but sets up a microbial universe that gives rise to to a plurality
cues.zh: 还建立起一个微生物宇宙，催生出多种多样的

cues.en: of other organisms.
cues.zh: 其他生物。

cues.en: I first proposed in the early nineteen nineties that mycelium is Earth's natural Internet.
cues.zh: 我在二十世纪九十年代初首次提出，菌丝体是地球的天然互联网。

cues.en: When you look at the mycelium,
cues.zh: 当你观察菌丝体时，

cues.en: there are...
cues.zh: 会有……

cues.en: Is... They're highly branched.
cues.zh: 是……它们高度分枝。

cues.en: And if there's one branch that that that is broken,
cues.zh: 如果有一条分支断了，

cues.en: then very quickly, because of the nodes of crossing,
cues.zh: 那么很快，由于交叉节点，

cues.en: Internet engineers maybe call them hot points, there's alternative pathways for channeling nutrients
cues.zh: 互联网工程师也许把它们叫作热点，那里有替代路径来输送养分

cues.en: and information.
cues.zh: 和信息。

cues.en: The mycelium is sentient.
cues.zh: 菌丝体是有感知的。

cues.en: It knows that you are there. When you walk across landscapes,
cues.zh: 它知道你在那里。当你走过地表时，

cues.en: it leaps up in the aftermath of your footsteps trying to grab debris.
cues.zh: 它会在你脚步过后迅速跃起，试图抓住碎屑。

cues.en: So I believe the invention of the computer Internet is an inevitable consequence
cues.zh: 所以我相信，计算机互联网的发明是一种必然结果

cues.en: of a previously proven biologically successful model.
cues.zh: 源自一个此前已被证明在生物学上非常成功的模型。

cues.en: The earth invented the computer Internet for its own benefit,
cues.zh: 地球为了自身的利益发明了计算机互联网，

cues.en: and we now, being the top
cues.zh: 而现在我们，作为这个星球上

cues.en: organism on this planet,
cues.zh: 最高等的生物，

cues.en: is trying to allocate
cues.zh: 正在尝试调配

cues.en: resources in order to to protect the biosphere.
cues.zh: 资源来保护生物圈。

cues.en: Going way out, dark matter conforms to the same mycelial archetype.
cues.zh: 再往宏观了说，暗物质也符合同样的菌丝原型。

cues.en: I believe matter begets life. Life becomes single cells. Single cells become strings. Strings become chains. Chains network.
cues.zh: 我相信物质孕育生命。生命变成单细胞。单细胞变成串。串变成链。链连接成网络。

cues.en: And this is the paradigm that we see throughout
cues.zh: 这就是我们在

cues.en: the universe.
cues.zh: 整个宇宙中看到的范式。

cues.en: Most of you may not know that fungi were the first organisms to come to land. They came to land one point three billion years ago, and plants followed several hundred million years later. How is that possible?
cues.zh: 你们大多数人可能不知道，真菌是最早登陆的生�物。它们在十三亿年前来到陆地，植物则在几亿年之后才跟上来。这怎么可能呢？

cues.en: It's possible because the mycelium produces oxalic acids and many other acids and enzymes.
cues.zh: 这是因为菌丝会产生草酸以及许多其他的酸和酶。

cues.en: Pop marking rock and grabbing calcium
cues.zh: 它侵蚀岩石，攫取钙

cues.en: and other minerals and forming calcium oxalates
cues.zh: 和其他矿物质，形成草酸钙，

cues.en: makes the rocks crumble
cues.zh: 使岩石碎裂，

cues.en: in the first step in the generation of soil.
cues.zh: 这是土壤形成的第一步。

cues.en: Oxalic acid is two carbon dioxide molecules joined together.
cues.zh: 草酸是两个二氧化碳分子结合在一起的产物。

cues.en: So fungi and mycelium sequester carbon dioxide in the form of calcium oxalates,
cues.zh: 所以真菌和菌丝以草酸钙的形式固存二氧化碳，

cues.en: and all sorts of other oxalates are also sequestering
cues.zh: 而通过从岩石基质中形成并析出的各种矿物质，其他各类草酸盐也在固存

cues.en: carbon dioxide through the minerals that are being formed and taken out of the rock matrix.
cues.zh: 二氧化碳。

cues.en: This was first discovered in 1859. This is a photograph by Franz Huber.
cues.zh: 这一现象最早在1859年被发现。这是一张Franz Huber拍摄的照片。

cues.en: This photograph was taken in nineteen fifties from Saudi Arabia. Four hundred and twenty million years ago,
cues.zh: 这张照片拍摄于二十世纪五十年代，地点在沙特阿拉伯。四亿两千万年前，

cues.en: this organism existed. It was called prototaxites.
cues.zh: 存在着这样一种生物。它被称为原杉藻（Prototaxites）。

cues.en: Prototaxites,
cues.zh: Prototaxites，

cues.en: laying down, was about three feet tall.
cues.zh: 平放时大约三英尺高。

cues.en: The tallest plants on earth at that time were less than two feet.
cues.zh: 当时地球上最高的植物不到两英尺。

cues.en: Doctor. Boyce at the University of Chicago
cues.zh: 芝加哥大学的 Boyce 博士

cues.en: published an article in the Journal of Geology this past year determining
cues.zh: 去年在《Journal of Geology》上发表了一篇文章，确定

cues.en: that Prototaxides
cues.zh: Prototaxides

cues.en: was a giant fungus,
cues.zh: 是一种巨型真菌，

cues.en: a giant mushroom.
cues.zh: 一种巨型蘑菇。

cues.en: Across the landscapes of Earth were dotted these giant mushrooms
cues.zh: 地球的景观中点缀着这些巨型蘑菇

cues.en: all across most land masses,
cues.zh: 遍布大多数陆块，

cues.en: and these existed for tens of millions of years.
cues.zh: 它们存在了数千万年。

cues.en: Now, we've had several extinction events, and as we march forward sixty five million years ago, most of you know about it, we had an asteroid impact.
cues.zh: 我们经历过几次灭绝事件，而时间来到六千五百万年前——你们大多数人知道这件事——我们遭遇了一次小行星撞击。

cues.en: The Earth was struck by an asteroid. A huge amount of debris was jettison into the atmosphere.
cues.zh: 地球被一颗小行星撞击，大量碎片被抛入大气层。

cues.en: Sunlight was cut off,
cues.zh: 阳光被遮蔽，

cues.en: and fungi
cues.zh: 而真菌

cues.en: inherited the earth.
cues.zh: 继承了地球。

cues.en: Those organisms that paired with fungi were rewarded,
cues.zh: 那些与真菌结成伙伴的生物得到了回报，

cues.en: because fungi do not need light.
cues.zh: 因为真菌不需要光。

cues.en: More recently, at Einstein University, they just determined
cues.zh: 更近些时候，在 Einstein University，他们刚刚确定

cues.en: that fungi use radiation as a food... As a as a source of energy, much like plants use light.
cues.zh: 真菌把辐射当作食物……当作一种能源，很像植物利用光。

cues.en: So the prospect of fungi existing on other planets elsewhere, I think, is a foregone conclusion, at least in my own mind.
cues.zh: 所以，真菌存在于其他星球上的前景，我认为已是定局，至少在我自己看来是这样。

cues.en: The largest organism in the world is in Eastern Oregon. I couldn't miss it. It was 2,200 acres in size.
cues.zh: 世界上最大的生物在俄勒冈州东部。我不可能错过它。它有 2,200 英亩大。

cues.en: 2,200 acres in size, 2,000
years old, the largest organism on the planet is a mycelium mat, one cell wall thick.
cues.zh: 年历史，地球上最大的生物是一块菌丝体垫，只有一个细胞壁那么厚。

cues.en: How is it that this organism
cues.zh: 这个生物怎么会

cues.en: can be so large and yet be one cell wall thick, whereas we have five or six skin layers that protect us. The mycelium in the right conditions produces a mushroom. It bursts through with such ferocity it can break asphalt.
cues.zh: 能如此巨大，却只有一个细胞壁厚，而我们却有五六层皮肤保护自己。菌丝体在合适条件下会长出蘑菇。它会以极大的力量破土而出，甚至能顶破沥青。

cues.en: We were involved in several experiments. I'm going to show you six, if I can, solutions for helping to save the world. Mattel Laboratories and I joined up in Bellingham, Washington. There were four piles saturated
cues.zh: 我们参与了好几项实验。如果可以的话，我想给大家展示六种拯救世界的方法。我和 Mattel 实验室在华盛顿州贝灵厄姆展开了合作。那里有四堆饱含

cues.en: with diesel and other petroleum waste. One was a control pile.
cues.zh: 柴油和其他石油废料的土堆。其中一堆是对照组。

cues.en: One pile was treated with enzymes.
cues.zh: 一堆用酶处理。

cues.en: One pile was treated with
cues.zh: 一堆用

cues.en: was treated with bacteria. And our pile, we inoculated with mushroom mycelium.
cues.zh: 细菌处理。而我们那一堆，接种了蘑菇菌丝体。

cues.en: The mycelium absorbs the oil. The mycelium is producing enzymes, peroxidases,
cues.zh: 菌丝体吸收了油污。菌丝体会产生酶，比如过氧化物酶，

cues.en: that break carbon hydrogen bonds.
cues.zh: 能够分解碳氢键。

cues.en: These are the same bonds that hold hydrocarbons together. So the mycelium becomes saturated with the oil.
cues.zh: 这正是把碳氢化合物结合在一起的同一种化学键。于是菌丝体吸饱了油污。

cues.en: And then when we returned six weeks later, all the tarps were removed, all the other piles were dead, dark and stinky. We came back to our pile. It was covered with hundreds of pounds of oyster mushrooms, and the color changed to a light form.
cues.zh: 六周后我们回去时，所有的防水布都已掀开，其他几堆全都死气沉沉、又黑又臭。回到我们的土堆，上面长满了数百磅的平菇，颜色也变浅了。

cues.en: The enzymes remanufactured the hydrocarbons into carbohydrates,
cues.zh: 这些酶把碳氢化合物重新转化成了碳水化合物，

cues.en: fungal sugars.
cues.zh: 也就是真菌糖类。

cues.en: Some of these mushrooms are very happy mushrooms. They're very large.
cues.zh: 其中一些蘑菇长得非常欢实，个头很大。

cues.en: They're showing how much nutrition that they could have obtained. But something else happened, which is an epiphany in my life. They sporulated. The spores attract insects. Insects laid eggs.
cues.zh: 它们展示了自己能从中获取多少养分。但还发生了另一件事，这成了我人生中的一次顿悟：它们孢子化了。孢子招来了昆虫，昆虫产下了卵。

cues.en: Eggs
cues.zh: 卵

cues.en: became larvae. Birds then came
cues.zh: 孵化成了幼虫。随后鸟类飞来，

cues.en: bringing in seeds, and our pile became an oasis of life.
cues.zh: 带来了种子，我们的土堆变成了一片生命的绿洲。

cues.en: Whereas the other three piles were dead, dark and stinky. And the PAHs,
cues.zh: 而另外三堆依然死气沉沉、又黑又臭。并且多环芳烃，

cues.en: the aromatic hydrocarbons,
cues.zh: 也就是芳香族碳氢化合物，

cues.en: went from 10,000 parts per million to less than 200
cues.zh: 的含量在八周内

cues.en: in eight weeks.
cues.zh: 从百万分之10000降到了不到200。

cues.en: The last image we don't have, the entire pile was a green berm of life. These are gateway species, vanguard species that open the door for biologicals... For other biological communities.
cues.zh: 最后一张图我们没有拍到，整个堆积物是一片绿色的生命之堤。这些是门户物种、先锋物种，为生物……为其他生物群落打开大门。

cues.en: So I invented
cues.zh: 于是我发明了

cues.en: burlap sacks, bunker spawn, and putting the mycelium using storm blown debris.
cues.zh: 麻袋、掩体菌种，以及利用风暴吹来的碎屑放置菌丝体。

cues.en: You can take these burlap sacks and put them downstream from a farm that's producing e coli or other waste, or a factory with chemical toxins, and it leads to habitat restoration.
cues.zh: 你可以把这些麻袋放到产生大肠杆菌或其他废弃物的农场下游，或者有化学毒素的工厂下游，从而促进栖息地恢复。

cues.en: So, we set up a site in Mason County, Washington,
cues.zh: 于是，我们在华盛顿州梅森县设立了一个站点，

cues.en: and we've seen a dramatic decrease in the amount of coliforms.
cues.zh: 我们发现大肠菌群数量显著下降。

cues.en: And I'll show you a graph here. This is a logarithmic scale, 10 to the eighth power is more than a 100,000,000 colonies per gram, and 10 to the third power is around a thousand. In forty eight hours to seventy two hours, these
cues.zh: 这里我给大家看一张图。这是对数刻度，10 的 8 次方是每克超过 1 亿个菌落，10 的三次方大约是 1000。在 48 到 72 小时内，这些

cues.en: three mushroom species reduced the amount of coliform bacteria
cues.zh: 三种蘑菇使大肠菌群细菌的数量减少了

cues.en: 10,000 times.
Think of the implications.
cues.zh: 想想这意味着什么。

cues.en: This is a space conservative method that uses storm debris, and we can guarantee... Be guaranteed that we'll have storms every year.
cues.zh: 这是一种节省空间的方法，利用风暴带来的碎屑，而且我们可以保证……保证每年都会有风暴。

cues.en: So this one mushroom in particular, Drew, has drawn our interest over time. This is my wife, Dusty, with a mushroom called Fomitopsis Officinalis Agaricon.
cues.zh: 所以，特别是这种蘑菇，Drew，长期以来一直吸引着我们。这是我妻子 Dusty，她拿着一朵叫 Fomitopsis Officinalis Agaricon 的蘑菇。

cues.en: This mushroom grows in Washington state, Oregon, Northern California, British Columbia, now thought to be extinct in Europe.

cues.en: Preserving the genome of these fungi in the old growth forest, I think, is absolutely critical for human health.
cues.zh: 我认为，保存原始森林中这些真菌的基因组，对于人类健康至关重要。
